chapter: Chicago friends: Tesch, Stacy and Wettling
title: Bringing Jess Stacy to Europe
summary: Freeman says European pianists imitate Stacy and discusses his agent bringing American stars over and whether Stacy would tour.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, the marvelous thing, if Jess could get to know, and this eventually he will, I suppose, hear this and read it, he's -- all the pianist I have
played with in Europe, say in Holland, Germany, the U. K. especially, Ireland, did I say Switzerland, Italy, are trying to play place that Jess Stacy style.
Bud, wouldn't it be nice if Jess did come over --
I think it's a shame that he doesn't come over. He would be a big thing over here.
He never really had it on his own like that. If he did it with you...
It might be a little frightening. Well, it's difficult -- my agent handles about eight big American stars, such as people like Teddy Wilson --
Robert Masters -- he doesn't handle Teddy but he handles Benny Carter from time to time, Buddy Tate, Lockjaw Davis --
No, it's Robert Masters, and he would love that idea. He brings Ralph Sutton over.

Yes, and what's the other pianist's name, Dick Wellstood, they have been very successful here. And he would love to bring Jess, I know, but he couldn't couple Jess with anybody else because it would be too expensive. But Jess could do very well on a tour,
it would be a very big thing, because his name is big now.
Of course, he may --maybe his personal affairs will be such that -- it's a great pity not to.
